'''Fred Irvin Diamond''' (born November 19, 1964)<ref name="cv"/> is a [[mathematician]], known for his role in proving the [[modularity theorem]] for [[elliptic curve]]s.<ref name="bbc"/> His research interest is in [[modular form]]s and [[Galois module|Galois representations]].

==Life==
Diamond received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1984,<ref name="kcl"/> and received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mathematics from [[Princeton University]] in 1988 as a [[doctoral student]] of [[Andrew Wiles]].<ref name="kcl"/><ref name="mg"/> He has held positions at [[Brandeis University]] and [[Rutgers University]], and is currently a professor at [[King's College London]].<ref name="kcl"/>

Diamond is the author of several research papers, and is also a coauthor along with [[Jerry Shurman]] of ''A First Course in Modular Forms'', in the [[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] series published by [[Springer-Verlag]].<ref>Review of ''A First Course in Modular Forms'' by Daniel Bump (2005), ''SIAM Review'' 47 (4): 813–816, {{JSTOR|20453715}}.</ref><ref>Review of ''A First Course in Modular Forms'' by [[Henri Darmon]] (2006), {{MR|2112196}}.</ref><ref>Review of ''A First Course in Modular Forms'' by [[Fernando Q. Gouvêa]] (2007), ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'' 114 (1): 85–90, {{JSTOR|27642138}}.</ref>
